newsitem.title: USA: Gelman Sciences Q1 hurt by inventory cuts. [CORRECTED 15:45 GMT 03/12]
newsitem.headline: Gelman Sciences Q1 hurt by inventory cuts. [CORRECTED 15:45 GMT 03/12]

text.p: Microfiltration products maker Gelman Sciences Inc said on Monday sales growth was slowed by reductions in customer inventories in the fiscal 1997 first quarter ended October 31.
The inventory reduction and sales shortfall was due partially to uncertainty among distributors, customers and employees due tothe company's merger plans, Gelman said.
The company initially announced a plan to merge with Memtec Ltd before deciding in October to merge with Pall Corp.
Sales growth was also cut by 0.8 percent (corrects from eight percent) by the effects of a stronger dollar, Gelman said, adding that consolidation in the healthcare industry also hurt sales.

The company reported sales of $28.3 million in the quarter, compared with $27.3 million a year ago. The net loss for the quarter was $2.9 million, or $0.36 a share, compared with a profit of $1.9 million, or $0.24 a share a year ago.

The first quarter loss was the result of a $3.6 million after-tax charge, or $0.45 a share, resulting from the payment of a termination fee to Memtec and other costs associated with the termination of the merger with Memtec, the company said.

"Although the first quarter results are lower than expected, I believe that our investments in our core membrane technology will positively impact the remainder of this fiscal year both in terms of downstream product quality and new product introductions," Gelman chief executive officer Charles Gelman said. "In addition, our merger with Pall should result in many synergies, including improved sales growth opportunities due to Pall's broad geographic sales distribution capabilities, and the ability to access its strong resource base."
Gelman shares fell 3/8 to 31-3/8 on the American Stock Exchange Monday.
